report_metadata.sdlc_rationale: Requirements are fully defined with explicit scope (expense submission, approval workflow, QuickBooks export), fixed deadline (10 weeks), fixed budget ($60,000), and named team composition (2 developers, 1 designer). No indication of evolving requirements or technology uncertainty.

project_understanding.primary_goal: Build an internal expense management portal enabling employees to submit expenses with receipt attachments, track reimbursement status, and allowing managers to approve/reject submissions with automated export to QuickBooks.
project_understanding.beneficiary: All employees (approx 300) and finance team (6 people)
project_understanding.trigger: Finance team needs a centralized expense management system to replace manual processes and improve reimbursement tracking.
success_definition: Employees can submit expenses with receipt attachments
Managers can approve or reject submissions
Reimbursement status is visible to submitters
Monthly reports export to QuickBooks without manual intervention
supporting_quotes: Employees should be able to submit expenses, attach receipts, and track reimbursement status
Finance exports monthly reports to our accounting system (QuickBooks)

assumption_log.what: Security authentication will use company SSO (single sign-on) rather than local username/password
assumption_log.why: Internal tool for 300+ employees requires centralized identity management; SSO is standard for enterprise internal systems
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 5.4 — Scope baseline requires accepted requirements; security architecture is foundational
assumption_log.consequence: If SSO is not available or required, authentication layer must be redesigned and re-implemented, adding 2-3 weeks to Phase 2
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: aligns with enterprise security standards and reduces credential management burden. Risks: if SSO is not available or company uses different auth method, architecture must pivot.

assumption_log.what: QuickBooks integration will use the QuickBooks Online API (cloud-based) rather than desktop QuickBooks
assumption_log.why: QuickBooks Online is the modern standard for business accounting; desktop integration is legacy and less common in new projects
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 11.2 — Risk identification before planning baseline; external API availability is a technical dependency
assumption_log.consequence: If company uses QuickBooks Desktop, integration approach changes entirely (may require middleware or manual export), adding 3-4 weeks to Phase 3
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: allows Phase 3 integration planning to proceed with modern API assumptions. Risks: if company uses Desktop version, integration complexity and timeline increase significantly.

assumption_log.what: Data retention policy: expense records retained for 7 years (standard for financial audit compliance)
assumption_log.why: Financial records typically require 7-year retention per IRS and SOX compliance standards for internal systems handling reimbursement data
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 5.4 — Scope baseline; compliance requirements affect architecture
assumption_log.consequence: If actual retention requirement differs (shorter or longer), database storage architecture and archival strategy must be redesigned
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: allows database design to proceed with standard retention assumptions. Risks: if company has different compliance requirement, storage and archival design must change.

assumption_log.what: QA Engineer (dedicated role) will be provided by shared services or hired as contractor, since input explicitly states 'developers will validate their own work' but does not name a QA resource
assumption_log.why: PMBOK 8.2 requires QA effort minimum 25% of development hours; developer self-testing alone does not meet quality standards for a 300-user internal system. Staffing plan must include dedicated QA to meet this baseline.
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 8.1 — Quality metrics defined before build begins; PMBOK 8.2 — Quality assurance requires independent verification
assumption_log.consequence: If QA resource is not available, test coverage will be insufficient, critical bugs will reach production, and reimbursement data integrity will be at risk. Rework and hotfixes will consume 20-30% of Phase 4 and Phase 5 effort.
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: ensures independent test coverage and compliance with quality baseline. Risks: if QA resource is unavailable, project must either delay to hire/contract QA or accept HIGH quality risk (flagged in risk_register as R4).

critical_path_summary.staffing_implication: Backend Developer and QA Engineer must be allocated full-time (100% and 80% respectively) with zero flexibility; any slip on API design, QuickBooks integration, or UAT will delay production deployment.

phases.name: Discovery & Design
milestones: Requirements document finalized and signed off by finance stakeholders
UI/UX wireframes approved by finance team
Security and data retention requirements documented

tasks.name: Conduct stakeholder interviews with finance team and sample employees to validate requirements
tasks.definition_of_done: Interview notes documented, key requirements confirmed, sign-off email from finance lead received

tasks.name: Design expense submission and approval workflow UI mockups
tasks.definition_of_done: Wireframes for submission form, approval dashboard, and status tracking page reviewed and approved by finance team

tasks.name: Document API specifications for QuickBooks Online integration and authentication flow
tasks.definition_of_done: API spec document includes endpoint definitions, data mapping, error handling, and authentication method; reviewed by tech lead

tasks.name: Create database schema design for expenses, approvals, and audit trail
tasks.definition_of_done: Schema diagram with all tables, relationships, and indexes documented; 7-year retention policy incorporated

phases.name: Core Development
milestones: Internal demo completed with finance team

tasks.name: Implement user authentication (SSO integration) and role-based access control
tasks.definition_of_done: Users can log in via SSO, employee and manager roles are enforced, access control tested for all user types

tasks.name: Build expense submission form frontend with receipt upload capability
tasks.definition_of_done: Form accepts expense details, file upload works, validation rules enforced, form submits to backend API

tasks.name: Implement approval workflow backend (state machine for pending/approved/rejected)
tasks.definition_of_done: Approval state transitions working, notifications sent to managers and employees, audit trail recorded

tasks.name: Build approval dashboard frontend for managers
tasks.definition_of_done: Dashboard displays pending expenses, allows approve/reject actions, shows approval history

tasks.name: Implement reimbursement status tracking and employee dashboard
tasks.definition_of_done: Employees can view submitted expenses and current status, status updates reflect approval workflow state

phases.name: Integration & Edge Cases
milestones: QuickBooks integration tested with sandbox data
Error handling and retry logic implemented

tasks.name: Implement QuickBooks Online API integration for monthly expense export
tasks.definition_of_done: Export process reads approved expenses, maps to QuickBooks format, sends to QuickBooks API, handles errors and retries

tasks.name: Implement receipt file storage and retrieval (cloud storage integration)
tasks.definition_of_done: Receipt files uploaded and stored securely, retrievable by authorized users, virus scanning enabled

tasks.name: Test QuickBooks integration with sandbox environment and validate data mapping
tasks.definition_of_done: Sample expenses exported to QuickBooks sandbox, data verified field-by-field, error scenarios tested (API down, rate limit, schema mismatch)

tasks.name: Implement edge case handling (duplicate submissions, concurrent approvals, large file uploads)
tasks.definition_of_done: Duplicate detection working, concurrent approval conflicts resolved, file upload limits enforced

tasks.name: Security review: authentication, authorization, data encryption, and compliance audit
tasks.definition_of_done: Security checklist completed, encryption at rest and in transit verified, audit trail immutability confirmed, compliance with 7-year retention policy validated

phases.name: QA & Testing
milestones: UAT completed with finance team and sample employees
Performance testing at 300+ concurrent users passed

tasks.name: Execute comprehensive functional test suite (submission, approval, export workflows)
tasks.definition_of_done: All test cases executed, critical bugs logged and fixed, regression testing passed

tasks.name: Conduct user acceptance testing (UAT) with finance team and sample employees
tasks.definition_of_done: UAT sign-off from finance lead, employee feedback documented, any critical issues resolved

tasks.name: Performance testing: load test at 300+ concurrent users, measure response times and throughput
tasks.definition_of_done: Load test results show < 2s response time at 300 concurrent users, no errors under load, database queries optimized

tasks.name: Accessibility testing and remediation (WCAG 2.1 AA compliance)
tasks.definition_of_done: Automated accessibility scan passed, manual keyboard navigation tested, screen reader compatibility verified

tasks.name: Deploy to production and execute smoke tests
tasks.definition_of_done: Application deployed to production, smoke tests passed, monitoring and alerting active

tasks.name: Write operational runbooks and post-launch support documentation
tasks.definition_of_done: Runbooks cover common issues, escalation procedures, and backup/recovery steps; finance team trained

risk_register.description: QA resource not named in input; developers will self-test. If dedicated QA engineer is not available from shared services or contractor, test coverage will be insufficient for a 300-user system, and critical bugs will reach production.
risk_register.trigger: QA resource request denied or unavailable; developers begin Phase 2 without independent QA support
risk_register.mitigation: Secure written commitment from shared services or contract QA engineer before Phase 2 begins. Establish QA allocation at 80% minimum for Phases 3-4.
risk_register.contingency: If QA is unavailable, extend Phase 4 by 2 weeks and allocate one developer (50%) to QA duties; accept HIGH quality risk and flag for post-launch hotfix budget.

risk_register.description: QuickBooks Online API integration is a critical external dependency. If API contract is not confirmed, sandbox access is delayed, or API schema differs from assumptions, Phase 3 integration will slip by 2-3 weeks.
risk_register.trigger: QuickBooks API documentation unavailable, sandbox access not granted, or API rate limits are lower than expected
risk_register.mitigation: Confirm QuickBooks API access and documentation in Phase 1 (T3). Test with sandbox data before Phase 3 begins. Document rate limits and error handling upfront.
risk_register.contingency: If API access is delayed, implement manual export CSV template in Phase 3 as fallback; automate QuickBooks sync in Phase 2 post-launch.

risk_register.description: SSO authentication integration is assumed but not confirmed. If company uses a different authentication method (LDAP, custom auth, or no SSO), Phase 2 authentication implementation must be redesigned, adding 2-3 weeks.
risk_register.trigger: IT confirms company does not use SSO or uses non-standard authentication method
risk_register.mitigation: Confirm authentication method with IT security team in Phase 1 (T3). Validate SSO sandbox access before Phase 2 begins.
risk_register.contingency: If SSO is unavailable, implement local authentication with password reset flow; extend Phase 2 by 1 week.

risk_register.description: Timeline is 10 weeks (11.5 weeks with 15% buffer). Critical path is 57.5 days (8.2 weeks). If any critical path task (T1, T3, T5, T8, T12, T15, T18) slips by more than 3 days, production deployment will miss the 10-week target.
risk_register.trigger: Any critical path task exceeds estimated effort by >20%, or external dependency (QuickBooks API, SSO) is delayed
risk_register.mitigation: Allocate Backend Developer and QA Engineer at 100% and 80% respectively. Schedule critical path tasks in weeks 2-9 (avoid week 1 ramp-up and week 10 deployment freeze). Weekly status reviews on critical path tasks.
risk_register.contingency: If critical path slips, reduce Phase 4 UAT scope (finance team only, no employee sample group) and extend Phase 5 by 1 week.

risk_register.description: Scope is well-defined but stakeholder sign-off is not explicitly mentioned in input. If finance team changes requirements mid-project (e.g., adds approval hierarchy, multi-currency support, or integration with other systems), scope creep will consume 2-3 weeks.
risk_register.trigger: Finance team requests new features or changes approval workflow after Phase 1 sign-off
risk_register.mitigation: Obtain written scope sign-off from finance lead at end of Phase 1 (T1). Establish change control process: any scope change requires timeline or budget adjustment.
risk_register.contingency: If scope creep occurs, defer non-critical features to Phase 2 post-launch and adjust timeline accordingly.

risk_register.description: Team size is small (2 developers, 1 designer). If either developer is pulled to another project or becomes unavailable, critical path tasks (T3, T5, T8, T10, T12) will have no backup, and timeline will slip by 2-4 weeks.
risk_register.trigger: Developer is reassigned to another project, becomes ill, or leaves the company
risk_register.mitigation: Secure written commitment from management that both developers are 100% allocated to this project for 11.5 weeks. Identify backup developer from shared pool before Phase 2 begins.
risk_register.contingency: If developer becomes unavailable, hire contractor backend developer immediately; extend Phase 2 by 1 week for onboarding.

risk_register.description: System handles financial data (expense reimbursement) and must comply with 7-year retention policy and audit trail requirements. If compliance requirements are not enforced during build, post-launch remediation will be costly and time-consuming.
risk_register.trigger: Audit discovers missing audit trail, data retention policy not enforced, or encryption not implemented
risk_register.mitigation: Include compliance requirements in Phase 1 scope (T1, T3). Conduct security review in Phase 3 (T14). Validate audit trail immutability and retention policy in Phase 4 (T15).
risk_register.contingency: If compliance gaps are discovered in Phase 4, allocate 1 week to remediation before UAT.

risk_register.description: Receipt file upload and storage is a new capability for the team. If file handling, virus scanning, or cloud storage integration is not properly implemented, security vulnerabilities or data loss could occur.
risk_register.trigger: File upload fails, virus scanning is not enabled, or files are not retrievable after upload
risk_register.mitigation: Use managed cloud storage service (AWS S3, Azure Blob) with built-in virus scanning. Implement file size limits and type validation in Phase 2 (T6). Test file retrieval in Phase 3 (T11).
risk_register.contingency: If file storage fails, implement temporary local storage with manual backup to cloud; extend Phase 3 by 3 days.

staffing_plan.notes: Owns requirements gathering, stakeholder alignment, UAT coordination, and post-launch handoff. Must be available for weekly status reviews and critical decision-making.

Critical path: owns API design (T3), authentication (T5), approval workflow (T7), QuickBooks integration (T10), and edge case handling (T13). Must be 100% allocated; no shared projects. Backup developer identified before Phase 2.

Owns submission form (T6), approval dashboard (T8), and status tracking (T9). Supports accessibility testing (T18). Can be shared with other projects at 40% if needed, but Phase 2 requires 80% allocation.
Front-loaded: owns UI/UX design (T2) in Phase 1-2. Can be allocated to other projects at 84% after Phase 2 ends.

CRITICAL: Assumed from shared services or contractor (not named in input). Owns QuickBooks integration testing (T12), functional testing (T15), performance testing (T17), and accessibility testing (T18). Must be 80% allocated in Phases 3-4. QA effort (100h) = 25% of development effort (240h + 180h = 420h × 25% = 105h minimum). Actual allocation meets baseline.
Assumed from shared services or security team (not named in input). Owns security review (T14) in Phase 3. Can be allocated part-time (20%) for 1 week.
Back-loaded: owns production deployment (T19) in Phase 5. Can be allocated part-time (20%) for 1 week. Assumes infrastructure (servers, databases, cloud storage) is pre-provisioned.

open_questions.question: Is a dedicated QA Engineer available from shared services or will one need to be hired/contracted? Input states 'developers will validate their own work,' but PMBOK 8.2 requires QA effort minimum 25% of development hours for quality assurance.
open_questions.impact_if_unanswered: If QA resource is unavailable, test coverage will be insufficient, critical bugs will reach production, and reimbursement data integrity will be at risk. Rework and hotfixes will consume 20-30% of Phase 4-5 effort, and go-live will slip by 2-3 weeks.

open_questions.question: Has the finance team formally approved the scope (expense submission, approval workflow, QuickBooks export) in writing, or is Phase 1 sign-off still pending?
open_questions.impact_if_unanswered: If scope is not formally approved, mid-project changes (e.g., approval hierarchy, multi-currency, additional integrations) will consume 2-3 weeks and delay deployment.

open_questions.question: Does the company use QuickBooks Online (cloud-based) or QuickBooks Desktop? Integration approach and timeline depend on this answer.
open_questions.impact_if_unanswered: If company uses QuickBooks Desktop, integration approach changes entirely (may require middleware or manual export), adding 3-4 weeks to Phase 3 and delaying deployment.

open_questions.question: What authentication method does the company use: SSO (single sign-on), LDAP, or local authentication? Phase 2 implementation depends on this.
open_questions.impact_if_unanswered: If SSO is not available, authentication layer must be redesigned and re-implemented, adding 1-2 weeks to Phase 2 and delaying downstream phases.

open_questions.question: Are both developers committed to 100% allocation for the full 11.5-week timeline, or are they shared with other projects? Any part-time allocation will break the critical path.
open_questions.impact_if_unanswered: If developers are shared or part-time, critical path tasks will slip, and deployment will miss the 10-week target by 2-4 weeks.
